glossary.definition: Attention is the part of a transformer that decides which words in a sentence matter most to understanding any given word. In the sentence "The trophy didn't fit in the suitcase because it was too big," attention is how a model figures out that "it" refers to the trophy, not the suitcase, by weighing which earlier words are most relevant. It works a bit like a spotlight operator at a play, dimming the words that don't matter right now and shining light on the ones that do.

items.title: OpenAI and rival AI labs are buying tens of thousands of Mac minis to train computer-use agents
items.summary: According to The Information, OpenAI has purchased tens of thousands of Mac minis and Mac Studios to train computer agents. Anthropic also relies on Apple hardware. Demand is so high that the most powerful models have been sold out for months. Apple’s Mac revenue rose by nearly 29 percent to $10.4 billion in the June quarter.

items.title: DiDi Starts Driverless Trials With R2 Robotaxi in Beijing and Guangzhou
items.summary: DiDi Autonomous Driving began fully driverless passenger service trials with its next-generation Robotaxi, the R2, on August 31, 2026, making the vehicle bookable through the DiDi App in selected demonstration areas of Beijing and Guangzhou, the company announced. The R2 is jointly developed by DiDi Autonomous Driving and GAC Aion. DiDi described the vehicle as purpose-built for Robotaxi service and designed for global deployment, with upgrades in autonomous driving performance and cabin experience over the prior generation. The R2 runs on DiDi Autonomous Driving’s Level 4 full-stack software and hardware.

items.title: The U.S. is building barriers around drones and robots, but China has scale to get around them
items.summary: S. is shutting out more foreign-made drones and robots. China’s scale means the global competition may simply move elsewhere. In July and August, Washington tightened restrictions on foreign-made advanced robotic systems and imposed steep tariffs on imported drones and their components, both moves citing national-security concerns. The drone tariffs take effect in September, with additional component tariffs following in 2027.

items.title: Musk’s faster path to more gas turbines comes with pollution problem
items.summary: Elon Musk says a secretive new SpaceX foundry will let him cast his own turbine blades and get gas power online 18 months faster than anyone else — but it's a bet on a fuel source that's already triggering lawsuits and health studies everywhere his (and others') turbines have gone in. Elon Musk says he’s found a way to solve one of AI’s biggest bottlenecks by making a hard-to-manufacture turbine part himself. “SpaceX and Tesla are each building 100GW/year of solar production capacity as fast as possible,” Musk wrote on X on Saturday, “but natural gas will still be needed to supplement and bootstrap solar for several years. The limiting factor for nat gas turbine production is casting the blades & vanes.

items.title: Texas Governor Abbott blocks funding for more Flock cameras
items.summary: As backlash grows over Flock's AI surveillance cameras, Texas Governor Greg Abbott has frozen state spending on them. The move came just ahead of the publication of a Texas Tribune investigation that revealed the state spent over $30 million on Flock cameras. That money was primarily raised by tacking a $1 fee onto insurance policies, allegedly to help fight catalytic converter theft. Flock cameras have increasingly drawn ire from across the political spectrum as they've become the subject of privacy concerns.

items.title: Why the next wave of AI startups won’t optimize infrastructure – until they have to
items.summary: For most AI startups, infrastructure isn’t the first problem to solve; speed is. At the earliest stages, success is defined by how quickly a team can move from idea to product, from prototype to traction. The constraints are immediate and unforgiving: limited runway, small teams, and the constant pressure to prove value before the next funding milestone. Startups don’t win at the earliest stage by minimizing cost per token or optimizing silicon performance.

items.title: Four safeguards to stop your AI agents from going rogue
items.summary: Artificial intelligence agents are moving from experimentation to production, and with this shift, the stakes are rising. A coding agent at PocketOS recently deleted an entire production database. An agent at Meta exposed sensitive user data for two hours. An Instagram support chatbot allowed hackers to hijack thousands of accounts. And last month, researchers tricked a GitHub agent into leaking private repository data.

items.title: AI sentiment is turning sour as employee reviews reveal growing frustration across the workforce
items.summary: An analysis of Glassdoor reviews shows that positive AI comments have dropped from 81 to 43 percent since 2019. Executives rate AI mostly positive, while insurance claims workers rate it almost entirely negative. Fear of job loss is just one complaint among many. Forced adoption, surveillance, and unrealistic productivity expectations weigh just as heavily. An analysis of employer reviews on Glassdoor shows that workers are becoming more critical of AI in the workplace.

items.title: What Is Agentic AI? How Systems Plan, Use Tools, and Complete Tasks
items.summary: Agentic AI systems do more than generate an answer: they pursue goals through a loop of planning, tool use, observation, and adaptation. Here is how that loop works, where agents add value, and what keeps them under control. Agentic AI is artificial intelligence that can pursue a goal by deciding what to do next, using tools, observing the result, and adjusting its approach. Instead of producing one response and stopping, an agent operates through a control loop until it completes the task, reaches a limit, or hands the work back to a person.

items.title: Why the Hottest New Wearables Want to Be Ignored
items.summary: Burnt out on wrist buzzes and notification overload? A new crop of minimalist wearables promises to collect your health data without demanding your attention. There’s a new kind of gadget on shelves, designed for you to ignore it 99 percent of the time—it only needs attention when its battery is low. I'm talking about the screen-free wearable .

items.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
items.summary: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell have filed suit against Anthropic in the US District Court for the Northern District of California seeking damages for "tens of thousands" copyrighted works. The companies are asking for up to $150,000 per work, plus up to $25,000 for each instance when identifiable copyright data was stripped. In total, the damages could amount to several billion dollars if a court finds in Sony and Warner's favor and awards the maximum amount. This is just the latest high-profile suit against Anthropic, which recently settled a suit brought by the publishing industry for $1.5 billion .

items.title: The Cybersecurity Apocalypse Is Coming in ‘Months,’ AI Giants Warn
items.summary: Plus: Hackers target over 100 US water systems, ICE puts in an order for robot dogs, and you’ll never guess what “MrChildPorn” was arrested for. You may have noticed that Flock Safety’s automatic license plate reader cameras—and the cops who misuse them—are getting a lot of coverage lately. This week, WIRED found a particularly wild case : A cop in Alpharetta, Georgia, was accused of searching for the license plate of a coworker dozens of times after an affair between the two ended, according to internal documents obtained by WIRED. The same police department where the former lovers worked also shared the data captured from its Flock cameras with more than 2,000 police departments, colleges, and other organizations across the United States, and accessed data from more than 1,300 entities in exchange.
